rationale: Both rewrite the byte-level state machine as a clean line-by-line renderer. Each tracks only whether a list is open and includes helpful refactoring notes. B is a little cleaner. Its headerLevel helper returns (level, ok), so a line with seven or more '#' falls through naturally to the paragraph case. A instead has renderHeading emit a paragraph itself. B detects list items with the precise '* ' prefix. A treats any line starting with '*' as a list item and then trims '* ', so a line like '*foo' would become a list item. B keeps the simple strings.Replace calls for emphasis. A adds a hand-written replaceFirstPair helper that only re-implements the same behaviour, which is needless complexity. B's use of WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(...)) where fmt.Fprintf would do is a minor nit. Overall B is marginally simpler and more precise.
